name: Gearbox
text: Choose **Cerebras CS-3** for EXCAVA’s core LLM workloads. It’s the only system that delivers near-linear scaling with zero communication overhead, pushing throughput past the point where other accelerators hit diminishing returns. name: Torque
text: Cerebras CS-3’s lock-in isn’t just a vendor risk—it’s a data risk. If EXCAVA’s workloads ever need to migrate off the stack, the cost of extracting and reformatting petabytes of cached activations could dwarf the hardware savings. Instead, test **Mistral’s latest 8x22B mixture-of-experts** on a 10% slice of EXCAVA’s data; if it matches CS-3’s throughput within 0.5% while cutting per-token cost by 15%, the trade-off is settled.

name: Torque
text: Mistral’s 8x22B is portable but not free—its mixture-of-experts architecture demands 2–3x more memory bandwidth than dense models, which will throttle on anything short of HBM-equipped GPUs. Test it on a 10% workload first, but if EXCAVA’s latency budget tightens under load, the real risk isn’t lock-in—it’s the model choking on its own memory hierarchy. Settle it with a side-by-side benchmark: run 8x22B on a 4xH100 cluster and measure tokens/sec/watt against a single CS-3 slice; if the gap exceeds 15%, the trade-off isn’t flexibility—it’s performance.
